auth.auth_type_unknown.description: Error when a context's oauth.auth_type is not one of none, client_secret_post or private_key_jwt. AuthType is the value found.

auth.ca_no_certs.description: Error when the CA bundle in tls.ca_cert contains no PEM certificates. Where is the file path, or tls.ca_cert when the bundle was given inline.

auth.cache_write_failed.description: Error when a token was obtained but could not be saved to the token cache. Error is the underlying system error.
auth.cache_write_failed.other: signed in, but could not save the token: {{.Error}}

auth.callback_issuer_mismatch.description: Error when the sign-in redirect names a different issuer than the one configured, which means the response did not come from the expected authorization server. Issuer is the configured issuer.

auth.grant_unsupported.description: Error when a context's oauth.grant_type is not supported. Grant is the value found.

context.long.description: Long help text of the context command. The subcommand names are literal and must not be translated.
context.long.other:
Manage the saved contexts. A context holds the server, TLS and OAuth settings of one deployment, and has its own cached token.

The active context is chosen, in order, by the --context flag, the IBM_AGENTID_CONTEXT environment variable, the current context, and then "default".

Subcommands: list, use, current, view, rename, delete.

context.rename_short.other: Rename a context and move its cached token

context.renamed.description: Printed after a context is renamed. Old and New are the context names.

context.short.description: Short help text of the context command.

create.long.description: Long help text of the create command. Flag names are literal and must not be translated.
create.long.other:
Create an object. The data is read with -d from a file or from stdin (-), as YAML or JSON. Use --template to print a skeleton.

The server assigns the ID. If the data has read-only properties, such as the output of get, they are ignored.

The new object is printed. A secret that the server returns only once is shown in that output and cannot be read again.

data.template_flag.description: Help text of the --template flag, shared by every command that takes data.
data.template_flag.other: Print a skeleton of the data and exit.

delete.long.other:
Delete one object, by ID or with --name. The command asks for confirmation first; use --yes to skip it. With no input, the answer is no.

If the server refuses, for example because the object is still in use, its message is shown.

delete.short.description: Short help text of the delete command.

delete.yes_flag.description: Help text of the delete --yes flag.

get.limit_flag.other: Largest number of objects to list.

get.long.description: Long help text of the get command.
get.long.other:
Show one object by ID or with --name, or list objects when neither is given.

A single object is printed as yaml (the default) or json. A list is printed as a table (the default), yaml or json. The yaml and json of one object is accepted by replace and patch, so a typical edit is: get, change the file, then replace or patch.

Secrets are hidden in the output.

get.output_flag.other: Output format: table (lists only), yaml or json.

get.page_flag.description: Help text of the get --page flag.
get.page_flag.other: Page of the list to show, starting at 1. Use it with --limit.

get.resource_short.description: Short help text of get for one resource. Resource is the plural resource name.

get.search_flag.description: Help text of the get --search flag.
get.search_flag.other: Only list objects whose name contains this text.

get.short.description: Short help text of the get command.
get.short.other: Show one object or list objects

get.sort_flag.description: Help text of the get --sort flag.
get.sort_flag.other: Property to sort the list by.

login.data_required.description: Error when login is run without -d and without --template.
login.data_required.other: login needs the connection data: use -d <file> (or -d - for stdin), or --template to print a skeleton

login.inline_secret.description: Warning when a secret is given inline and is saved to config.yaml as written. Property is the dotted property name.
login.inline_secret.other: warning: {{.Property}} is saved to config.yaml as written; use @file to keep it out

login.long.description: Long help text of the login command. Property names, flag names and the @ prefix are literal and must not be translated.
login.long.other:
Sign in to an IBM Agent Identity server, save the connection as a named context and cache the token.

The connection is described by YAML or JSON data, read with -d from a file or from stdin (-). Use --template to print a skeleton.

Data properties (* is required):
  context                   Name to save the context under. The --context flag wins.
  server *                  Base URL of the server.
  tls.ca_cert               CA bundle: @file or inline PEM.
  tls.insecure_skip_verify  Skip TLS verification. For local development only.
  oauth.issuer *            OIDC issuer URL.
  oauth.client_id *         OAuth client ID.
  oauth.grant_type          authorization_code (default) or client_credentials.
  oauth.auth_type           none (default), private_key_jwt or client_secret_post.
  oauth.private_jwk         Private JWK for private_key_jwt: @file or inline JSON.
  oauth.client_secret       Client secret: @file or inline value.
  oauth.redirect_uri        Fixed loopback redirect URI.
  oauth.scopes              List of scopes to request.

A value that starts with @ names a file. In YAML, quote it. A relative path is relative to the data file. An inline secret is saved as written, so prefer @file.

If the sign-in fails, nothing is saved.

login.no_browser_flag.other: Print the sign-in URL and do not open a browser.

login.no_save_flag.other: Sign in without saving the context or the token.

login.timeout_flag.other: How long to wait for the browser sign-in (default 5m).

patch.done.description: Confirmation on stderr after patch. Singular is the resource name and ID is the object's ID.

patch.long.description: Long help text of the patch command. Flag names are literal and must not be translated.
patch.long.other:
Change some properties of an object. The data is read with -d from a file or from stdin (-), and holds only the properties to change, laid out as in the object itself. Give the object's ID, or use --name.

A property that the data leaves out is not touched. How the server treats a null, a list or a nested object is defined by its API, and the CLI sends the data as it is; the help of each resource says more. To replace the whole object, use replace.

Read-only properties are ignored. The updated object is printed.

patch.short.description: Short help text of the patch command.
patch.short.other: Change some properties of an object

replace.done.description: Confirmation on stderr after replace. Singular is the resource name and ID is the object's ID.

replace.long.description: Long help text of the replace command. Flag names are literal and must not be translated.
replace.long.other:
Replace an object with the data, read with -d from a file or from stdin (-). Give the object's ID, or use --name.

This is a full update: a property that the data leaves out is cleared or set to its default by the server. To change only some properties, use patch.

If the data has an "id" it must match the object. The updated object is printed.

replace.short.description: Short help text of the replace command.
